item: A process that is stopped while a backup snapshot is still being written removes the snapshot, on a double SIGINT and on a SIGTERM that outlasts the graceful window
summary: MEASURED, case by case, on a real uvicorn and the real app. A cancel while a snapshot is written (the native task.cancel a server applies, an anyio cancel scope) is clean: two whole-app tests pin it. SIGINT twice closed the loop with no task left, the interpreter waited for the non-daemon worker and exited 0 with .oo-backup-*/snapshot.db, a plaintext copy of the corpus, in the data folder: an atexit hook over a pid-stamped table of the directories this process made now removes it (Python joins non-daemon threads before exit hooks; a forked child never removes its parent's download). One SIGTERM whose 30 s graceful window runs out during a snapshot, or while a client that stopped reading holds the response, is NOT clean: uvicorn cancels the task, restores the default handler and re-raises, and the process dies by the signal (rc -15, no join, no hook), leaving the copy (8 s snapshot against a 2 s window; a finished 54 MB snapshot against the production 30 s). That is the in-app power button, SIGHUP, a plain kill or service stop. install_stop_signal_cleanup(), called in _serve() before uvicorn.run, installs the handler uvicorn restores and re-raises into: it removes this pid's directories, restores SIG_DFL and signals itself, so the exit status stays -15. The earlier text of this item, and the first correction of it, were inferred from reading the code and are corrected in place in the lesson. Real-process tests for each case with the handler-less control (leaves the directory), handler unit tests, a source-order test for _serve, and mutants for the hook, the registration, the forget-on-release, the pid guard and the handler. A kill (SIGKILL, power) runs nothing: item 40.
